content.text:
`harshgupta-mem0` isn't a collaborator on the repo; that account doesn't even have push access. It shows in the contributors list because of one commit:

```
72ba1fa  harshgupta-mem0 <harsh.gupta@mem0.ai>  "first commit"
```

GitHub links any commit made with `harsh.gupta@mem0.ai` to `harshgupta-mem0`. To remove it from the list, you have to change that commit's author and force-push. It's the root commit, so all 8 commit SHAs in the repo will change.

**Steps** (run them as `harsh-madhav`; the `gh` here is logged in as `harshgupta-mem0`, which can't push):

```bash
# 1. Fresh clone
git clone git@github.com:harsh-madhav/upshift.git /tmp/upshift-fix && cd /tmp/upshift-fix

# 2. Rewrite the author on every commit that used the mem0 email
git filter-branch --env-filter '
if [ "$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL" = "harsh.gupta@mem0.ai" ]; then
  export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="harsh-madhav"
  export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="harsh.madhav.gupta@gmail.com"
fi
if [ "$GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL" = "harsh.gupta@mem0.ai" ]; then
  export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="harsh-madhav"
  export GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="harsh.madhav.gupta@gmail.com"
fi' -- --all

# 3. Check that no mem0 email is left
git log --format='%h %an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>' --all

# 4. Force-push
git push --force --all
git push --force --tags
```

(If you have it installed, `git filter-repo --mailmap` does the same job more cleanly.)

**Things to know:**
- **Cache delay:** GitHub caches the contributors list, so it can take from a few hours to a day or so to update after the push.
- **Other copies:** Any existing clone, fork or open PR will be based on the old history. Re-clone instead of pulling into an old copy.
- **Stop it happening again:** Set your personal identity in your local upshift clone with `git config user.email harsh.madhav.gupta@gmail.com`. That stops new commits being credited to the mem0 account.

I didn't run any of this, because force-pushing rewrites the repo's public history. If you want, I can do it once `gh`/git is authenticated as `harsh-madhav`.

content.text:
The rewrite worked. The new `main` (8 commits, from root `70cfb81` to tip `87c36c9`) no longer contains the mem0 email anywhere. `git log --all` still showed `72ba1fa` because `filter-branch` keeps a backup of the old history under `refs/original/`. That backup is never pushed.

The push failed because the SSH key on this Mac belongs to `harshgupta-mem0`, and so does the `gh` login. You need to push once as `harsh-madhav`. The quickest way is HTTPS through `gh`:

```bash
cd /tmp/upshift-fix

# Add your personal account to gh (opens the browser; log in as harsh-madhav)
gh auth login -h github.com -p https -w
gh auth switch -u harsh-madhav     # only needed if it didn't become active
gh auth setup-git

# Push over HTTPS instead of SSH
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/harsh-madhav/upshift.git
git push --force origin main

# Switch back to your work account afterwards
gh auth switch -u harshgupta-mem0
```

There are no tags in the repo, so you don't need `--tags`.

After the push, go to github.com/harsh-madhav/upshift/commits/main. The latest commit should be `87c36c9` and the first one `70cfb81`. The contributors list in the sidebar can take a few hours to a day to drop `harshgupta-mem0`.

If you push to personal repos often from this Mac, a more permanent fix is a separate SSH key for `harsh-madhav` with a host alias in `~/.ssh/config`. I can set that up if you'd like.
